subject: Transportation Systems
title: Air Traffic Management for Drones
description: A quick, practical guide to Air Traffic Management for Drones.

hook.text: Hundreds of drones and air taxis flying over a city at once need a traffic control system that doesn't exist yet.

buildup.text: Traditional air traffic control uses human controllers and radar. That model can't scale to thousands of low-altitude flights.

discovery.text: NASA and the FAA are developing UTM—Unmanned Traffic Management—a digital system for automated flight routing.

twist.text: UTM must handle weather changes, emergency diversions, and no-fly zones in real time without human oversight.

climax.text: Without UTM, urban air mobility can't scale. It's the invisible infrastructure that makes everything else work.

punchline.text: The sky needs traffic rules. We haven't written them yet.

quiz.question: What is UTM?
options: Unmanned Traffic Management for low-altitude digital air traffic control
